ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $2.76 to the rider for the unexplained off-route distance; no account flag (no prior upheld route dispute in 90 days).
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the meter moves with distance and any unexcused extra distance is charged to the rider. RD-1 is satisfied: the trace confirms one off-route segment [F3], where 3.50 km was driven against 1.54 km of optimal route, adding 1.96 km, up to 752 m off the optimal path. Under RD-2 the refund is the sum of the extra_km of the non-exempt segments multiplied by this trip's per-km rate taken from the fare record ($33.33 ÷ 23.64 km = $1.4099/km) [F3][F4][F6], rounded to cents.

RD-4(a) does not exempt the segment. The driver asserts a breakdown and points to the LTA feed [F8], and a vehicle-breakdown incident does exist at 18:27, 0 m from the optimal route [F11]; that element passes on location and timing. The trace nevertheless marks RD-4(a) as failed because the substitute route's own condition was not slow: the only speed bands on the corridors are band 5 (40–49 km/h), which is not band 1 or 2 [F9][F10], and under RD-4(b) a speed band alone would not exempt a segment in any event. Weather was fair, so no other reasonable cause appears [F12].

RD-5 is the rider's branch, and it turns on the record of what was said, not on the driver's account [F8]. The fact table contains no in-app chat messages between rider and driver at all [F7], so there is no rider message sent before 18:46:55 agreeing to any route, and a driver's claim of agreement appearing only in his post-trip statement is not consent [F8]. A complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment therefore counts under RD-5; the segment is not exempt and is refundable under RD-2.

RD-3 does not apply either: no stop is measured within the segment, and the only place the driver's statement names is an alternative way, not a rider-requested stop [F3][F8].

RD-6 is not triggered: the driver profile shows route disputes upheld in the last 90 days = 0, so this case does not make the breach "repeated" and no account flag is raised [F14].

Amount: the segment's extra_km is 1.96 km; 1.96 km × $1.4099/km = $2.7634, rounded to $2.76 [F3][F4][F6]. The tariff-rate figure is independently cross-checked: the fare record bills $3.06 for 2.17 km, i.e. $3.06 ÷ 2.17 km = $1.4101/km, consistent with the trace's $1.4099/km rate [F4]. The residual excess in the fare record beyond the segments ($3.06 − $2.76 = $0.30) is movement within the 200 m route corridor and map-matching jitter, which RD-2 leaves with the rider [F1][F4]. Under NS-7 the refund is issued as a Ryde voucher and does not disturb the rest of the metered fare [F6].

The segment's extra 1.96 km is therefore not exempt and is refundable under RD-2.
